keyFindings.description: readIssue's issue-row callback returns pgx.ErrNoRows into batchResults.Close, so every 404 runs pgx 5.11's invalidateCachesOnBatchResultsError and drops all six batch statements (issueRowStatement among them, which loadIssue uses on other routes) from that connection's statement cache (the shared pool runs the default QueryExecModeCacheStatement, store.go:53). The old path ran one QueryRow and invalidated nothing. Fix: record the miss in the callback, return nil, and return pgx.ErrNoRows after Close.

loadOpenAsks (:509) and loadChildren (:680) have no production caller after this change; only issue_read_batch_test.go calls them. AGENTS.md:2693 says every other route still calls them, and AGENTS.md:2671 names loadChildren as the children read. Delete them and correct the docs; the test builds its reference from the shared statements and scans.

readIssueDetails re-implements loadArtifacts' versions-then-approvals sequence and the ask identity-event + backlink-count pair (a fourth copy), and refs/events now export a statement and its scan as separate symbols each caller must pair by hand (toKind twice, the empty-ids check, a size hint). Put queue-and-apply beside each lookup (artifact details, ask details, refs/events queue functions) and use them on both the batched and sequential paths.
issueRead mirrors getIssue's anonymous response struct, and the test declares it a third time; name the response type once.

TestIssueReadCostsTwoRoundTrips counts every statement on the traced pool; POST /issues in the new CITE project starts ensureSearchTermStats in the background (related_terms.go:445, not awaited) on that pool, which can land in the counted window. Count only the measured request's context. The sequential count asserts nothing.

stripSampleDoc holds no inline hard break and no line feed, so nothing pins writtenTree(node, false) in StripAnchorMarks; the tester showed true is unobservable on Parse output, but editor documents hold both.

proseFixedByReviewer: 35f52a9d: AGENTS.md and getIssue's comment said the pool refuses a second connection taken while a batch holds one; Pool.SendBatch sets no hold mark, so it would not. AGENTS.md's 'about eleven' statements became the real count (six, two with documents, two with open asks, one per artifact). The changelog's latency and share figures now quote this head's round-2 medians, as the PR body does.
handoff commit: AGENTS.md:2097 named readBackReaders, which this change removes; it names the three readers and readBackReaderCount.
